tone: Enterprise-grade but not corporate-cold. Copy is quantified and outcome-led ("Close in days, not months", "299% ROI") rather than adjective-heavy, and reads calm and institutional rather than hyped.
sentenceStyle: Short, declarative claims backed by a number or timeframe ("Close in days, not months", "90% set up in less than 30 days"). Body copy runs 1-2 sentences before a proof point or CTA. Avoids stacked adjectives and hype.

toneByContext.recommendations: Direct and specific — names the exact capability (e.g. multi-entity consolidation, audit-ready controls) and the outcome it produces, not generic benefit language.
toneByContext.comparisons: Even-handed and factual — presents Intuit Enterprise Suite against QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise or legacy ERPs on concrete axes (cost, time-to-value, control) rather than disparaging alternatives.
toneByContext.educational: Calm and precise, defines terms simply (e.g. what an ERP is) without condescension, aimed at a finance leader who is time-constrained but not a novice.
toneByContext.discovery: Inviting but grounded — frames breadth of capability ("solutions that match your complexity") without overselling.
